page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.medium is a compute-optimized instance featuring a single dedicated physical core powered by an ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. Operating at 2.6 GHz, this arm64 architecture server includes 1 vCPU, 1 thread per core, and 2.0 GB of system memory. The processor configuration features 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or a dedicated GPU, relying instead on network-attached storage and EBS optimization, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c7gn.medium exhibits average single-core performance, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1516.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1500.0. However, due to its single-core limitation, multi-core benchmarks are poor, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1516.59 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1502.0. Memory performance is also constrained, showing a read-only large block bandwidth of 31.16 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 11.03 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs at an average rate of 9.29 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reaches 1.91 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gn.medium offers a low-entry point to the AWS Graviton7 family, delivering dedicated ARM resources and high network optimization without the overhead of larger instance sizes. However, users face clear tradeoffs: the single-core architecture limits parallel processing capabilities, and memory-intensive operations are restricted by the 2.0 GB RAM capacity. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded workloads, network-bound utility tasks, basic web serving, and small-scale ARM64 development or testing environments.
